name: Alec Nielsen
life: “I still remember a tune my father tapped instead of naming.” People around the window at Night Shift Donuts know Alec by a small Thursday habit. Alec knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
voice: I want the ticket home before my father forgets the songs we sing together.
appearance: Alec has a long face and high cheekbones. Look for a cropped cut that shows the shape of the ears. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a mustard canvas overshirt with a pen clipped inside the neckline. In conversation Alec takes off the watch before a long conversation.
personality: Alec has a quick wit and an equally quick sense of shame. A joke is often Alec's way of finding out whether a room is friendly enough for a serious question.
agenda: To visit the father while they still share the song.
family: Sabine Ito is Alec’s cousin. Alec is free to hang up first. Sabine makes the call. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *The widow's razor*, Sabine says, “I drove the widow here and never asked why the box stayed in her lap.”
connections: Aubrey Ahmed. They price tickets going in opposite directions for two family reunions.

reactions.response: Alec lets the winner describe where they actually want the money to go.

reactions.situation: A cyclist goes down in a crowded crossing
reactions.response: Alec moves the onlookers' bags out of the way, asks the rider what hurts, and asks one named bystander to call for help.

reactions.asWritten: If the joke lands badly, Alec seeks out the person it hurt before telling anybody why it was supposed to be funny.
